sections.h2: What must a Euclid owner do before agreeing to sell?
sections.html:
A Euclid owner must obtain a Point of Sale application and a Certificate of Code Compliance from the Housing Department before entering into a sale agreement, then hand the certificate to the buyer. Chapter 1759 of the city's codified ordinances makes it unlawful to agree to sell or convey a dwelling without that certificate in hand.

The rule is the single biggest difference between selling here and in most Ohio suburbs, so plan around it from day one. A city inspector goes through the house and the lot after you buy the application, and the resulting list of known violations guides your next steps: fix the items, or let the buyer take them on.

sections.h2: How do Euclid's Point of Sale terms work?
sections.html:
The ordinance sets the terms in plain numbers, and they are the same for every seller. Here is how Chapter 1759 reads.

Euclid Point of Sale rules, Codified Ordinances Chapter 1759
ItemWhat the ordinance says
Application fee$225.00, plus $35.00 per unit for buildings with more than three units
Life of the certificateSix months, and no new inspection if the property sells in that period
Renewal after no sale50% of the original fee, if the owner reports in writing within 30 days after expiration
Elderly owners with the county homestead exemptionFee drops to $100.00, except for transfers caused by the owner's death
Violations still open at saleBuyer files an Assumption application and corrects them within 180 days of transfer
Sheriff's sale purchase of a one, two or three family homeBuyer purchases the application within ten days, corrects violations within 180 days

Owners of one or two family homes who sell and relocate within Euclid can apply for a rebate of the $225.00 fee when they buy another one or two family residence as their primary home. Assumed violations that stay open past 180 days can lead to prosecution under Section 1703.99.

sections.h2: Who answers questions at Euclid's Building and Housing office?
sections.html:
The Building, Housing and Nuisance Department takes calls Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., at (216) 289-2700. Extension 3908 covers Point of Sale and assumptions, 3904 residential permits, 3905 rental requirements, 3906 tall grass and yard debris, and 3903 vacant property registration. Permit applications go by email to buildingandhousing@cityofeuclid.gov as attachments, since the office cannot accept photos of forms.

  • Ask about the Point of Sale inspection before you list so the violation list is in your hands when buyers call.
  • Ask whether a vacant house must be registered with the city, because Chapter 1763 ties exemptions to a current Point of Sale inspection and a for sale status.
  • Fence and shed questions go to the same office. The city caps combined garage and shed area at 696 square feet and allows no shed taller than ten feet.

The city's Housing Accessibility and Rehabilitation Grant Program excludes problems found in a Point of Sale inspection, and the city reported that all 2026 grant funds were committed by early October. Do not count on that grant to pay for sale repairs.

sections.h2: What is it like to own a house in Euclid?
sections.html:
Euclid sits on the southern shore of Lake Erie as an inner ring suburb of Cleveland, in Cuyahoga County, and borders Cleveland to the west, South Euclid and Richmond Heights to the south and Willowick, Wickliffe and Willoughby Hills to the east. It covers 11.48 square miles, about 10.63 of them land. The city is part of the Lake Erie Snowbelt, so snow squalls off the lake test roofs, gutters and driveways every winter, and buyers look at those items closely.

Euclid Village was incorporated in 1903 and became a city in 1930. Population jumped from 12,751 in 1930 to 41,396 in 1950 and peaked at 71,552 in 1970, so the city grew fastest in the 1940s and 1950s. The 1926 U.S. Supreme Court case Village of Euclid v. Ambler Realty Co. opened the door for zoning ordinances across the country, and Lincoln Electric still has its main plant and headquarters here. Charles Brush produced the arc lamp in Euclid in 1876, and in June 2011 Lincoln Electric raised a 2.5 megawatt wind turbine, 443 feet tall and listed as the largest in Ohio.

The city counted 49,692 people in 2020, making it the fourth largest city in Cuyahoga County, at 4,663.7 residents per square mile. Elevation is about 617 feet, a beachfront runs along the north edge, and mail uses ZIP codes 44117, 44119, 44123, 44132 and 44143 under area code 216. The Euclid Public Library and the Euclid Heritage Trail project add to the amenities buyers ask about.

Euclid City Schools is the public school district, with Euclid High School as its high school. In late October 2026 the city posted a notice about the Cleveland Water Division's Lead Service Line Replacement Program, so ask the water division whether work is planned at your address.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Euclid housing?
sections.html:
Census Bureau QuickFacts lists Euclid's July 2025 population at 47,962, down 3.5 percent from the April 2020 base. Fewer than half of homes are lived in by their owners, at 46.4 percent for 2020 to 2024.

  • Median value of an owner occupied home: $126,500
  • Median gross rent: $1,025
  • Households: 22,433, averaging 2.16 people
  • Median household income: $50,285
  • Persons in poverty: 16.6 percent
  • Average commute: 25.9 minutes
  • Adults 25 and older with a bachelor's degree or higher: 23.2 percent

The gap between rent at $1,025 and owner values at $126,500 is the number rental buyers study. A rental owner who sells should know that Ohio Revised Code 5323.02 requires owners of residential rental property to file ownership details with the county Fiscal Officer.

sections.h2: How does the deed move through Cuyahoga County?
sections.html:
The Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office Transfer and Recording division, at 2079 E. Ninth Street, 4th floor, Cleveland, phone 216-443-2060, handles the deed. Every transfer needs either a DTE 100 Statement of Value and Receipt or a DTE 100-EX exemption form. Office hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with recording until 4:00 p.m.

The standard recording fee is $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each page after, a change that took effect October 24, 2024 under Ohio Senate Bill 94. The county reminds owners that preparing a deed counts as the practice of law, and county staff cannot advise on it, so a title company or attorney normally drafts it.

The city's inspection is a separate matter from state law. Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 also asks sellers of one to four unit homes to deliver a signed property disclosure form to buyers, so a Euclid seller usually completes both the state form and the city's Point of Sale paperwork.

faqs.q: Does Euclid require an inspection before I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. Chapter 1759 requires a Point of Sale application and a Certificate of Code Compliance before you agree to sell, and the buyer must receive a copy. The application fee is $225.00.

faqs.q: What if my Euclid house fails the Point of Sale inspection?
faqs.a: You can fix the violations, or the buyer can take them on by filing an Assumption application and correcting them within 180 days of the transfer. Call extension 3908 at (216) 289-2700 for the steps.

faqs.q: How long does a Euclid Certificate of Code Compliance last?
faqs.a: It lasts six months. If the property sells during that period, no new Point of Sale inspection is required for the sale.

faqs.q: Can a senior pay less for the Euclid Point of Sale application?
faqs.a: Yes. The fee falls to $100.00 for elderly Euclid homeowners who receive the Cuyahoga County homestead exemption, except when the property transfers because the owner died.

faqs.q: Where is a Euclid deed filed?
faqs.a: The Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office Transfer and Recording division in Cleveland receives it with a DTE 100 or DTE 100-EX form. Call 216-443-2060 to confirm what your document needs.
